title: An HTML Canvas Graphics Device
text: result standalone HTML file: open browser, plot drawn live browser’s canvas engine JS commands R’s graphics engine produced. can inspect generated commands directly:
code: library(cnvs)  f <- tempfile(fileext = ".html") cnvs(f, width = 480, height = 400) plot(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars, col = "steelblue", pch = 19,      main = "mtcars: mpg vs weight") abline(lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars), col = "firebrick", lwd = 2) invisible(dev.off()) cat(readLines(f)[8:18], sep = "\n") #> <canvas id="cnvs-page-1" width="480" height="400" style="border: 1px solid #ccc; margin-bottom: 1em;"></canvas> #> <script> #> (function() { #>   var canvas = document.getElementById("cnvs-page-1"); #>   var ctx = canvas.getContext("2d"); #>   ctx.fillStyle = "rgba(255, 255, 255, 1.000)"; #>   ctx.fillRect(0, 0, 480, 400); #>   ctx.save(); #>   ctx.beginPath(); #>   ctx.rect(78.72, 78.72, 360.96, 223.36); #>   ctx.clip();

FALSE, <canvas>/<script> block page written, surrounding document; meant embedding output fragment inside larger HTML page already (instance, knitted Quarto R Markdown document), opening . id_prefix Base string used build page's <canvas> element id (page n gets id = paste0(id_prefix, "-", n)). default, "cnvs-page", fine single device writing file. Supply distinct value per device embedding one cnvs() fragment (standalone = FALSE) host HTML document – e.g. one call per code chunk Quarto/R Markdown document – <canvas> ids collide.
